newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money eases down an ample supply.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money eases down an ample supply.

text.p: Jakarta call money eased down to 10.0/10.5 percent from 14.0 percent on Thursday on the back of sufficient liquidity supply, dealers said.
They said central bank supply of 693 billion rupiah helped calm the market because operators remained cautious one day after a bank reserve requirement rate of five percent was made effective.
"Operators were a bit nervous at the opening, trading call money at a relatively high level. But sufficient supply seemed to have softened the market," one Japanese bank dealer said.
One-week money was last given at 12.75 percent and one-month edged down to 13.0 from 13.5 percent.
"I think the market would have normalised by next week. The central bank announced the new rate last year which gave plenty of time for banks to prepare," another dealer said.
Dealers said short-term swap rates also declined in line with the money market. Overnight swap was down to 0.95/1.1.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 15.19 percent, compared with 5.49 percent on Tuesday.
The market will be closed on Friday for a Moslem holiday and reopen on Monday.
The yield for PLN V/A bonds stayed at 14.9 percent.
